title: Minimax Estimation of the Population Fraction with Nonpositive Conditional Treatment Effect
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound matched point-risk and honest-length package subfield: paper score ceiling 7.0 is below the field threshold 7.4, with no same-scope salvage.
gap_reasons: The contribution is nevertheless confined to an engineered benchmark with known uniform two-dimensional design, fixed smoothness, a unique oriented transverse graph, and nonadaptive tuning, limiting its broader econometric significance.
The claimed observable confidence interval depends on an unspecified proof constant C_star, so it establishes minimax existence and order but is not yet a reproducibly calibrated procedure.

The load-bearing upper lemma also compresses the canonical U-statistic projection and dependency-graph moment accounting into assertions that require fuller auditable derivation, while the paper supplies no numerical implementation or benchmark demonstrating the estimator's practical behavior.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved a matched n^(-4/13) absolute-error minimax frontier and an honest expected-length frontier on the declared bounded-outcome, known-uniform two-dimensional class. The decision and math referees passed, but the general referee graded the delivered package subfield because its engineered fixed-smoothness single-graph benchmark did not meet the field-level paper-score threshold. Studentized calibration and broader design or smoothness regimes remain separate research directions; no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: For the population fraction with nonpositive CATE on the known-uniform square, with H\"older-\(1/4\) propensity and baseline regression, bounded outcomes in \([0,1]\), and a \(C^2\) transverse zero graph, the minimax absolute-error rate is \(n^{-4/13}\). The observable signed-root nearby-pair spline estimator attains it. For every fixed \(\alpha_0\in(0,1)\), a deterministic Markov interval centered at that estimator is uniformly honest and has optimal maximal expected length \(n^{-4/13}\); a finite-grid Bernoulli fuzzy experiment supplies the all-confidence-level lower bound. Studentized calibration and a uniform limit law remain open. This is a structured rough-confounding benchmark, not any anchor paper's published class verbatim.
gap: Munch and Gerds leave sublevel-probability minimax rates open. Chen and Gao settle moving-contour rates for direct regression, and Chen, Chen, and Gao analyze the same sign-share functional when both treatment-arm regressions are smoother than one. None of these results supplies an observable response or a sharp same-class frontier when the propensity and baseline regression are only H\"older-\(1/4\).
fill: The project pairs a nearby-pair spline estimator, whose nuisance bias is a product of local increments, with a uniform-design squared-bump mixture whose one-observation law cancels exactly. The intended result is a matching upper and lower absolute-error rate of \(n^{-4/13}\).
